chunks: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sulayman ibn Nahik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding His Exalted Saying: 'And We gave him refuge on a high ground of level ground and flowing water.' He said: 'The high ground is Najaf of Kufa, and the flowing water is the Euphrates.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Najaf and the Euphrates in this Quranic commentary?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* offers a distinctive Shia exegetical link between the Quranic description of divine refuge and the sacred geography of Najaf, identifying it as the 'Rabwah' (high, level ground) and the Euphrates as the 'Ma'in' (flowing water). This interpretation elevates the spiritual status of Najaf not merely as a burial site but as a locus of prophetic sanctuary, reinforcing the region's centrality in Shia devotional practice and geographical theology.
